data.title: Cuisinière: How the Gas Range Was Built

sentences.text: If you set a pot over an open fire, you have a stove.
But heat blasts out of the open flame and spreads across the room, and cooking causes roughly 44 to 49 percent of reported home fires.
So you box the fire in with steel walls and set the pot on a grate.
But now the trapped heat is all or nothing, so the soup boils over and runs down the front.
So you add a gas valve and a knob that turns the flame down.
Gas flows through the valve to the burner, and a rotten egg smell is added so you notice leaks.
The blue flame burns at about 1,960 degrees Celsius in air at most, so the knob matters.
And the gas stove is not a French invention, whatever the word cuisinière suggests.
It was an Englishman, James Sharp, who patented it in 1826.
Add an oven door, a pot lid and a hood with a light.
Congratulations, you have built a gas range.
